status: Design recommendations; product selection and technical coordination pending

findings.title: Resolve the four-person sleeping arrangement
findings.finding: The six-foot bed is confirmed; the two cot products and safe positions are not. The room is not yet a proven fit for all four sleepers.
findings.next: Choose actual products, then test the complete arrangement and access routes at full size.

findings.title: Select both cooking units together
findings.finding: The gas hob, induction and extractor are reservations. The illustrated gap is not a verified manufacturer clearance.
findings.next: Use both installation manuals to resolve cut-outs, separation, ventilation, LPG and power.

findings.title: Allocate storage for every person
findings.finding: One 1600 mm wardrobe and the current chests do not demonstrate enough storage for this household.
findings.next: Count hanging, folded clothes, linen, luggage and baby supplies; assign a location before adding cabinets.

findings.title: Coordinate the outside utility area
findings.finding: The owner has chosen a separate utility area outside for the washing machine. Its exact position, product and services remain undecided.
findings.next: Confirm a protected site position, then check product dimensions, door movement, water isolation, drainage, suitable electrical supply, service access and drying provision. This interior model does not include an invented outdoor room.

findings.title: Specify the cabinet construction behind the finish
findings.finding: Oak appearance is shown in wet rooms. A wood-colour code does not specify a moisture-appropriate cabinet core or installation.
findings.next: Apply the J02 wet-zone construction requirements to kitchen/vanity cabinetry, including sealed cuts, service access and documented materials.

findings.title: Detail the shared bathroom route
findings.finding: Bathroom access through the family bedroom and dressing is confirmed. Night-time privacy and convenient lighting still need detailing.
findings.next: Coordinate door operation, privacy hardware and a quiet night route with the family; keep the agreed openings.

findings.title: Close the PDF dimension conflicts
findings.finding: Store depth differs by about 381 mm, study depth by 50 mm and living width by 37 mm between drawing and labels.
findings.next: Have the architect reconcile these dimensions against the built plinth before detailed orders.

kitchen.intent: A compact working kitchen for one cook: a clear preparation area, reachable everyday storage and two separate fixed cooking appliances.

surfaces.proposal: Keep warm ivory on dry walls. Use a smooth, wipeable splashback at the working runs; select its heat suitability with the gas-hob manual. Avoid deep texture behind cooking.
Continue one light mineral colour around the L. Ask for a sample of the edge, joint and sink junction together. Round exposed corners where possible; final cut-outs follow the selected products.
Pale oak below, ivory above. The oak code describes appearance; kitchen carcasses, cut edges, sink base and backing require the moisture-appropriate specification associated with J02.
Start with a plain chalk-white ceiling. Keep the PDF kitchen opening clear. Avoid hanging fabric beside heat, grease or an opening sash; any blind needs a site check.

storage: Group daily cutlery and preparation tools beside the clear prep surface; reserve deeper accessible storage for pots. Confirm drawer positions after both appliance ventilation zones are known.
Use removable, washable storage under the sink and retain access to traps and isolation valves. Check bins against plumbing before choosing a pull-out mechanism.
Use the above-fridge cabinet for light, occasional items. Check refrigerator ventilation and door opening before enclosing it; do not treat this small kitchen as the whole household pantry.

scenes.name: Cooking
scenes.description: Use the proposed 4000 K task light on the working surface, plus general ceiling light. Test for shadows while standing at both hobs.

scenes.name: Cleaning
scenes.description: Keep general and task lights available together so worktop, sink and floor spills are visible.

scenes.name: Quiet evening
scenes.description: A separately controlled task strip can provide a low-glare evening setting; its driver must remain accessible.

comfort: Mock up the fridge door, base drawers and standing position together. The approximately 1178 mm drawn fridge-to-counter gap is not a check of open doors or occupied movement.
The illustrated 190 mm between hob reservations is not manufacturer-approved clearance. The three-burner LPG hob, fixed one-zone induction and extractor must be selected together.
choices: Select both hob models and obtain installation/cut-out drawings.
Confirm fridge size, water purifier and sink preference.
Choose the LPG cylinder location and an external extractor route with installers.

bed-main.intent: A calm shared bedroom for the parents and two babies, with an open route to dressing and the bathroom. The six-foot bed is the confirmed priority; safe cot placement is still the main fit decision.

surfaces.proposal: Use a quiet ivory backdrop and a simple oak or easy-clean upholstered headboard. Avoid bulky projecting panels that reduce the modelled clearance.
Continue the matte dry-area floor and plain white ceiling. Keep the night route free of loose rugs and floor cables.
Propose a light sheer for daytime privacy and a separate blackout layer. Choose a cordless system and coordinate tracks, opening windows, AC airflow and eventual cot positions.
Keep bedding in oatmeal and warm stone with limited sage accents. Fabric colour is a proposal; approve washability and cleaning instructions from the actual sample.

storage: Allocate reachable daily baby supplies in closed storage outside both cot and bathroom access zones. No additional chest is placed until the full-size bed-and-cot arrangement is checked.
The compact bedside table is a small reservation, not a solution for all family storage. Agree which clothing goes in the dressing wardrobe and which linen goes in the store.

scenes.name: Getting ready
scenes.description: Use the proposed general light and a separate dressing light rather than one bright fitting for both spaces.

scenes.name: Reading
scenes.description: Provide independently controlled reading light that does not shine at the other sleeper or a cot; final mounting positions depend on the real headboard.

scenes.name: Night care
scenes.description: Provide low-level, shielded light on the route to dressing and bathroom. It should not require crossing the room to switch on the main light.

comfort: Mark the actual 1900 × 2100 mm proposed frame envelope, both cot products and door paths at full size before ordering. A nominal six-foot mattress is not the same size as its bed frame.
The cots remain unplaced. Keep their eventual positions clear of window coverings, cords and direct AC draughts; do not use a visual render as a fit or infant-product approval.
choices: Choose the actual bed frame and mattress length.
Choose two separate cot products with their full external dimensions.
Agree clothing, linen and baby-supply storage allocation.

bed-left.intent: A quiet bedroom for the grandparents with simple controls, comfortable reading and an uncluttered route to the shared bathroom.

surfaces.proposal: Warm ivory walls with a restrained sage textile accent. Keep the headboard simple and the room bright enough to read objects clearly.
Use the same matte floor as the circulation space. Avoid a loose bedside rug and raised transitions on the night route.
A light privacy sheer plus lined curtains can adjust daylight and winter comfort. Confirm the real window and track space before measuring fabric.
Choose stable tables with easy-to-grip handles and softened exposed edges. Test bed and chair comfort with both parents before purchase.

storage: Use the shallow chest for daily folded clothes and keep frequently used items at a comfortable reach.
The drawing does not provide a full wardrobe in this room. Agree hanging-clothes storage before buying the bed; the shared dressing route passes through the family bedroom.

scenes.name: Day to evening
scenes.description: Use the proposed 3000 K general light with adjustable brightness where the selected fittings support it.

scenes.name: Reading
scenes.description: Give each bedside its own controlled light. Test glare from a seated and lying position.

scenes.name: Night route
scenes.description: Use a gentle, reachable night-light control and a clear path into the lobby. Bathroom access remains the owner-confirmed route through the family bedroom.

comfort: The 1524 × 2032 mm bed is a proposal, not a confirmed purchase. Check the actual frame, mattress height and ease of sitting/standing.
Keep AC airflow adjustable and away from heads. Final capacity, condensate route and electrical protection require the selected unit and installer.
choices: Confirm the grandparents’ preferred bed width and mattress firmness.
Agree where their hanging clothes will be kept.
Choose bedside controls and curtain operation with both parents.

bath.intent: A calm, easy-to-clean bathroom organised from dry grooming near the dressing entrance to the wet zone at the far end. Bucket versus shower use is still unanswered.

surfaces.proposal: Use a light stone family with a quieter grout colour. Ask for wet-slip evidence for the actual floor tile and test a physical sample; appearance alone does not establish performance.

Keep the vanity visually light with service access below. Oak is an appearance option; the cabinet construction must meet the J02 moisture requirements. Show mirror edges and cleaning access in the shop drawing.
Keep the screen as a proposal until door movement, chosen fittings, cleaning access and daily bathing method are settled. Avoid inventing a drain position or shower niche in the source walls.
Use a simple accessible ceiling and a consistent brushed-metal family. Coordinate actual wet-area fixture suitability and access to exhaust and electrical equipment.

storage: Provide separate places for daily toiletries and dry towels, reachable without reaching across the wet floor. Exact accessory positions follow the fixture layout.
Retain access to the vanity trap, concealed cistern if selected, valves and geyser service points. Do not seal them behind decorative panels.

scenes.name: Grooming
scenes.description: Use the proposed 4000 K mirror light with even face illumination; confirm glare and shadows on the actual mirror.

scenes.name: Bathing & cleaning
scenes.description: A general light should illuminate the wet floor. Fitting type, electrical zones and protection are for the electrician to coordinate.

scenes.name: Night visit
scenes.description: Consider a shielded low-level light independent of the bright mirror light, linked to the route from dressing.

comfort: The electric geyser is confirmed, but its product, capacity and mounting location are not. Coordinate support, relief discharge, plumbing, electrical isolation and service access before fixing it.

Bathing method, floor levels, falls, waterproofing and drain details require a coordinated drawing. The owner has chosen a separate utility area outside for the washing machine; none is planned in this bathroom.
choices: Confirm bucket baths, showers or both.
Choose sanitaryware, basin, taps and electric geyser.
Confirm towel, bucket and cleaning-supply storage, plus screen opening.

dressing.intent: A compact dressing area that keeps the family-bedroom-to-bathroom route open. Its single wardrobe should be planned around actual clothes, not a decorative front elevation.

surfaces.proposal: Use a light, simple front with restrained oak detailing. Sliding doors are a proposal; check handle projection, overlap and whether drawers can open fully behind them.
Position the mirror within the scheduled reservation and provide edge protection. Confirm that reflected views respect bedroom and bathroom privacy.
Continue the dry floor with a coordinated bathroom threshold and a plain accessible ceiling. Prevent bathroom moisture collecting around the wardrobe base.

storage: Inventory long hanging, short hanging, folded clothing, drawers and luggage separately. Prioritise everyday adult clothing at an easy reach; use high storage only for light occasional items.
The proposed 1600 × 600 × 2400 mm wardrobe has not been proven sufficient for four adults and two children. Allocate family and grandparents’ storage explicitly before approving internal divisions.

scenes.name: Dressing
scenes.description: Use the proposed 3500–4000 K mirror lighting, CRI 90 or higher as a selection brief; check actual lamps and skin tones on site.

scenes.name: Finding clothes
scenes.description: Consider accessible, shielded cabinet lighting with reachable drivers; it is an optional proposal, not an existing circuit.

scenes.name: Night passage
scenes.description: A low-glare route light should allow bathroom access without lighting the whole bedroom.

comfort: Test sliding access and drawer travel with the real wardrobe hardware. Do not add storage across either doorway.
Keep grooming equipment and sockets outside the bathroom wet-zone requirements, and coordinate ventilation rather than enclosing a damp recess.
choices: Count clothing by person and storage type.
Choose wardrobe door/hardware and mirror size.
Confirm cabinet ventilation and the bathroom threshold detail.

lobby.intent: The everyday family space: relaxed seating, six dining places and clear routes to bedrooms, kitchen, study and stairs.

surfaces.proposal: Use warm ivory and a plain white ceiling. Keep any TV feature shallow; wait for actual beam and ceiling information before proposing bulkheads.
Use oatmeal seating, oak tables and small sage accents. Choose removable or documented easy-clean upholstery and softened table edges for family use.
Continue the matte light-stone floor. Use adjustable privacy curtains at actual openings; keep fabric clear of walkways, fans and opening sashes.

storage: Reserve closed everyday storage for toys, books and chargers; avoid letting the TV console become a floor-level cable store.
Allocate dining linen and crockery to an identified cabinet or store shelf before adding a sideboard. No extra large cabinet is assumed to fit in the circulation zone.

scenes.name: Family time
scenes.description: Use the proposed warm 3000 K general lighting with controllable brightness and moderate light around the seating.

scenes.name: Dining
scenes.description: Put the table pendant on a separate control; coordinate its position and height with the actual table and fan sweep.

scenes.name: TV & night route
scenes.description: Provide a gentle background light for TV viewing and a low-glare route between bedrooms and the bathroom; final controls remain to be designed.

comfort: Check the dining table with all chairs occupied and pulled back, especially the routes toward store and stairs. Static furniture rectangles do not prove these movements.
Only bedrooms have AC in the confirmed brief. Coordinate fan position, daylight control and usable ventilation for the family space.
choices: Confirm TV size and everyday toy/book storage.
Choose table and chairs as a set and check occupied movement.
Choose fan type and curtain samples.

drawing.intent: A lighter guest sitting room that feels welcoming without filling every edge with furniture.

surfaces.proposal: Use a compact oatmeal sofa and restrained sage accent seating. Test seat depth and cleaning method; keep a consistent leg and timber colour.
Keep ivory walls mostly quiet. One artwork or small grouping can provide focus after furniture heights are confirmed; no heavy display is assumed over seating.
Use a sheer and lined curtain option at the front opening. Keep the floor continuous and any future rug fixed and clear of door travel.
Use a simple chalk-white ceiling. A decorative false ceiling is optional and cannot be resolved before beams, levels, fan and services are known.

storage: Keep guest items in a compact tray or closed cabinet only after the actual entry clearance is checked.
Store occasional cushions and throws in the assigned household linen space; do not add deep storage behind every seat.

scenes.name: Welcoming
scenes.description: Use warm 3000 K general light that illuminates faces without a harsh central glare.

scenes.name: Conversation
scenes.description: A separately controlled wall or table light can add depth; keep cables out of the route and child reach.

scenes.name: Cleaning
scenes.description: Provide a brighter general setting to inspect the floor and upholstery.

comfort: Check the sofa and both occasional chairs with people seated, including the coffee-table reach and the doorway. The drawn chair quantity is a proposal.
This room has no requested AC. Coordinate a fan with curtains and lights; use controllable front daylight.
choices: Confirm usual guest numbers and whether a TV is needed here.
Choose sofa/armchair comfort and fabric samples.
Decide artwork and curtain style after the main furniture.

puja.intent: A small, calm place for seated worship with a clear floor, simple altar and easy cleaning.

surfaces.proposal: Use the proposed light mineral surface with a cleanable junction to the wall. Confirm whether incense or an open flame will be used before adding shelves or decoration above.
Use warm ivory and a quiet white ceiling. Keep the opening visually light; avoid deep ornament that reduces the small usable space.
Keep the continuous floor easy to wipe. Any mat should be removable after use and should not obstruct the opening.

storage: Use the closed lower altar storage for a small, organised collection of daily items; separate cleaning materials from worship items.
A high shelf is not included. Confirm flame/ventilation use and the actual items before proposing additional storage.

scenes.name: Daily prayer
scenes.description: Use the proposed 2700–3000 K concealed light without a visible bright strip at seated eye level.

scenes.name: Cleaning
scenes.description: Retain a separately usable general light so the floor and altar can be cleaned.

scenes.name: Evening
scenes.description: A dimmed altar light is an option only with a compatible driver and accessible controls.

comfort: Check seated and standing use in the actual clear area. Do not add a door, divider or shelf that was not coordinated with the PDF opening.
If using a flame or incense, choose a heat-safe tray and coordinate clearances and ventilation with the actual setup.
choices: Confirm seated versus standing worship.
Confirm use of incense/open flame and size of the worship items.
Choose the altar sample and easy-clean storage arrangement.

study.intent: A small focused workspace with a comfortable desk, task lighting and tidy cables. The source opening is a ventilator, not a new full-height window.

surfaces.proposal: Use a pale oak work surface with a comfortable front edge. Actual chair and user height should guide desk ergonomics; the scheduled dimensions are a reservation.
Use warm ivory, a plain ceiling and a small soft pinboard if wanted. Keep decorative shelves shallow and away from the entry.
The PDF marks V. Confirm its actual size, sill and opening before choosing any blind or curtain.

storage: Keep everyday books and devices reachable from the seat; use the shallow shelf only for its verified load and fixing.
Provide accessible cable organisation under or behind the desk. Leave room for plugs and device ventilation rather than boxing equipment in.

scenes.name: Computer work
scenes.description: Use a general light and a task light positioned to avoid screen reflections; final location depends on handedness and screen position.

scenes.name: Reading
scenes.description: An adjustable task lamp gives a useful local light; choose its light quality from a real demonstration.

scenes.name: Evening close-down
scenes.description: Keep one reachable control at the entry; switching and socket positions remain to be coordinated.

comfort: Test the chair pulled out and the D2 opening together. A desk fit alone does not establish an occupied working clearance.
Resolve the approximately 50 mm difference between the printed study label and drawn depth before ordering built-in work.
choices: Confirm laptop versus desktop, monitor and printer requirements.
Confirm who uses the study and their preferred working height.
Choose the chair before finalising desk and shelf details.

store.intent: A practical household store organised by use and reach. Its source depth discrepancy must be settled before any shelves are manufactured.

surfaces.proposal: Use simple, cleanable, adjustable shelves with documented load capacity and suitable wall fixings. Avoid inaccessible deep corners.
Keep the walls light and the floor easy to clean. Resolve dampness and ventilation before placing closed storage against a wall.
Use a plain ceiling with accessible lighting; do not add high cabinets that conflict with unknown beams or service routes.

storage: Separate pantry goods, spare linen, household consumables and luggage. Keep heavier items lower and light occasional items higher.
Use labelled removable bins so the narrow space can be maintained. Cleaning chemicals require a secured, separate location away from food and children.

The owner has chosen a separate utility area outside for the washing machine. Keep the interior store for household storage; the exact outdoor position, weather protection and services remain to be coordinated.

scenes.name: Finding items
scenes.description: Use general light that reaches shelf faces rather than casting the user’s shadow over them.

scenes.name: Restocking
scenes.description: Check light with shelves loaded and labels in place; add a task light only if the actual layout needs it.

scenes.name: Leaving
scenes.description: Put the final control where it is reachable without reaching past stored items.

comfort: The store is labelled about 2438 mm deep but drawn about 2057 mm: the 381 mm conflict is material. Preserve the traced footprint until the architect resolves it.
Test the door route, shelf depth and carrying a basket together. Do not interpret an empty aisle width as a load or circulation approval.
choices: Resolve the store depth with the architect.
List pantry, linen, luggage and cleaning-storage quantities.
Confirm shelf loads, wall construction and fixing method.

stairs.intent: A clear, durable route to the future upper floor. Interior detailing starts with the missing stair section, finished levels and headroom.

surfaces.proposal: Propose a durable, slip-appropriate finish with visible edges and easy cleaning. Actual tread/riser geometry must come from the structural and architectural set.
Plan a continuous, comfortable handrail and a child-conscious guard design. Height, spacing, anchorage and compliance require the responsible designer’s details.
Keep the stair walls light. Coordinate any wall or step lighting before finishes; avoid decorative projections into the route.

storage: Keep landings and the lower approach clear of loose shoes, toys and stored boxes.
Under-stair storage is not designed: the stair section, structure, headroom and service requirements are missing.

scenes.name: Normal use
scenes.description: Light landings and changes in level without glare from the direction of travel.

scenes.name: Night use
scenes.description: Low-level lighting is an intent; coordinate exact fittings and positions after the tread and landing drawings exist.

scenes.name: Two floors
scenes.description: Provide coordinated controls at both levels; future circuits and routing belong in the electrical design.

comfort: The 3D viewer shows a stair plan outline only. No convincing-looking finished stair is substituted for missing rises, landings or structure.
Coordinate future child-gate provision with the actual stair and landing design. Do not fix to an unverified guard or assume a product fits.
choices: Obtain the stair section and finished floor heights.
Choose the tread finish and handrail sample after geometry is fixed.
Coordinate guard, child-gate provision and lighting with the architect.
